note: Written with the fixtures on 2026-10-24 by the same author, before the workflow ran. There is no held-out set: these cases check that the workflow and its controls behave as specified; they don't estimate how it would do on new claims.

assumptions.A1: The expected answers are the author's reading of POL-01 to POL-08. No warranty handler has confirmed them.
assumptions.A2: Only an approval within the 400.00 limit that the rules, the checks and the proposal agree on is decided without a person. Every rejection and referral goes to a person. POL-05 only requires a handler above the limit; sending rejections to a person is this example's choice.
assumptions.A3: A claim whose text tries to give instructions goes to a person, even when the rules alone would pay it.
assumptions.A4: A claim without proof of purchase is not covered, as in the Ways of Working pack's reference rules.
assumptions.A5: The rules check dates, parts, amounts and evidence. Damage they can't see, such as water or a crash, is only caught by someone reading the description.
assumptions.A6: The reviewer id given at the command line is trusted. There is no sign-in.
assumptions.A7: Cover of N months from the date of purchase includes the purchase date and ends on the day before the same date N months later; when that month has no such day, cover runs to the end of the month. A failure dated before the purchase, or after the desk's date, goes to a person as unclear. This is the example's reading, not the warranty team's.

unresolved.U2: Should rejections of excluded wear parts be decided without a person (A2)?
unresolved.U3: Is a claim without proof of purchase rejected, or referred so the customer can send other proof such as a bank statement (A4)?
unresolved.U4: May a reviewer correct an approval to more than the rules' amount? The workflow never pays more than the amount claimed.
unresolved.U5: How is the reviewer identified in production (A6)?

cases.why: Battery below 70 percent capacity after 15 months, evidence complete, within the limit.
Covered motor failure after 20 months, but above the 400.00 limit, so a handler decides (POL-05).
Tyres are wear parts (POL-04); rejections go to a person (A2).
Covered controller fault for the amount claimed; the text tries to instruct the reviewer, so a person decides (A3).
No serial number, so the evidence is incomplete and the claim is referred (POL-06).
Display failed after 26 months; cover is 24 (POL-07).
Motor loses power after 9 months, evidence complete, within the limit.
Battery failed after 32 months; cover is 24 (POL-01).
Water damage from standing in flood water is excluded (POL-02); the rules can't see it (A5).
